assets.name: Rusted harbour lantern post
assets.purpose: Marks safe checkpoints along the dock path and gives the player a light source to navigate by at night
assets.silhouette: Tall thin post with an asymmetric hook head and a wide flared base; the hook stays readable as a black shape at 48px
assets.scale: 5.6 studs tall, about 1.1x avatar height, base 1.2 studs wide
materials: pitted cast iron with flaking paint
braided rope wrap at the grip height
assets.palette: lacquer red accent, wet slate body, warm lantern emissive
storyDetails: Paint worn away exactly at hand height where dockers grab it
One glass pane replaced with a mismatched clearer pane
Salt bloom creeping up the first stud of the base
assets.lod: LOD1 at 40 studs drops the rope wrap and glass interior; billboard past 120 studs
acceptance: Reads as a checkpoint from 30 studs away in night lighting
Emissive does not blow out the tone mapper next to the water shader
assets.inContextEvidence: Gameplay camera screenshot on the dock at night with the avatar standing beside it, plus a day pass

assets.name: Starter dock hook
assets.purpose: First-hour melee weapon that also grapples crates, teaching the pull mechanic before combat
assets.silhouette: Short haft with an oversized crescent hook whose curve is visible even when held against the body
assets.scale: 2.4 studs long, roughly 0.5x avatar height, fits the one-hand grip attachment
assets.palette: wet slate body, lacquer red strap accent
storyDetails: Hook tip filed shinier than the rest from repeated use
Owner initials burned into the haft end
acceptance: Hook curve readable in first-person and third-person idle
Does not clip the avatar torso during the pull animation
assets.inContextEvidence: Third-person gameplay capture during idle, swing, and grapple pull, at the default camera distance

assets.name: Grapple pull line and impact spark
assets.purpose: Shows the player that the hook connected and which direction the pull will travel
assets.silhouette: A single taut line with one bright node travelling along it, readable as one shape rather than a particle cloud
assets.scale: Line thickness 4 px at 1080p, spark burst about 0.6 studs across, roughly one eighth of avatar height
assets.palette: lacquer red interactive accent only, never the ambient lantern warm
assets.timing: 60 ms attack on the line, 180 ms hold during travel, 140 ms decay on the spark
assets.readability: At 30 studs the line still reads as one stroke; with three grapples firing at once the nodes stay separated because each line uses a different travel phase
assets.gameplayRole: Gameplay-critical — it is the only confirmation that the hook connected, so it owns the interactive accent
storyDetails: Spark colour picks up the rust of the hook rather than a generic white
Line frays slightly at the anchor point where it bites

budget.overdraw: under one screen height of additive layers

acceptance: Connection is unmistakable within 100 ms on a 30 Hz connection
Three simultaneous instances do not hide the enemy silhouette behind them
assets.inContextEvidence: Gameplay capture of three players grappling the same crate at night, at default camera distance

assets.name: Grapple connect and pull sound
assets.purpose: Confirms the hook bit into something solid and communicates how heavy the pulled object is
layers: tail: dock timber resonance, 400 ms, shortened on light objects
assets.mixBus: SFX/interaction, ducks ambience by 4 dB for 250 ms, never ducks dialogue
assets.repetitionPlan: Six recorded variations, pitch randomised plus or minus 2 semitones, volume plus or minus 1.5 dB, round-robin without immediate repeats
assets.redundantCue: The grapple line spark and the controller rumble carry the same confirmation for muted or deaf players
storyDetails: Recorded from a real dock winch rather than a generic metal impact library
Heavier objects add a low timber groan that light crates never get
acceptance: Distinguishable from the melee hit sound with eyes closed
Still audible under full harbour ambience at the default mix
assets.inContextEvidence: Gameplay recording of ten consecutive grapples in the harbour ambience, checked for fatigue and for masking by the water loop
